description: We are Spectrum Explorers, a team for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge at NASA Space Apps 2026. Our goal is to blend space data, web dev, and astronomy to build an interactive platform visualizing near-infrared sky surveys to make cosmic data accessible and reveal shifting sky patterns.
summary: NASA’s SPHEREx telescope generates thousands of sky images every six months across 102 infrared wavebands, yet utilizing this massive data remains challenging due to sluggish web platforms and a lack of user guidance. BlinkSphere was developed to solve this by integrating dynamic tile-based loading to eliminate lag, seamless navigation across spectral bands and timeframes, an AI agent for automated celestial object detection, and advanced RGB-driven water mapping tools. This platform is vital because it empowers passionate students with an accessible, hands-on space exploration experience while easing the heavy processing workload for scientists through smart, efficient analytical tools.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

BlinkSphere (powered by our SPHEREx Spectral Lab engine) is an interactive, web-based astronomical platform built to simplify the exploration and analysis of massive hyperspectral telescope datasets, specifically targeting NASA’s SPHEREx mission. Instead of forcing users to download heavy raw files, BlinkSphere processes 3D spectral data cubes (128×128 spatial pixels across 102 infrared wavebands) and streams them smoothly to the browser using dynamic tile-based lazy loading. Users can seamlessly scrub through all 102 infrared bands and historical timeframes, generate custom RGB composite maps to detect water and ice signatures (H_2O and CO_2 absorption lines), and inspect individual celestial spectra in 2D and 3D. Additionally, an integrated AI anomaly-detection agent (using Isolation Forest) automatically flags unusual objects and classifies light sources against scientific reference templates (Pickles, EAZY, and Prism libraries).  

Key Benefits & Intended Impact

Traditional astronomical tools are sluggish, steep in learning curve, and resource-heavy. BlinkSphere eliminates platform lag and lowers the technical barrier to entry. Our intended impact is dual-fold:  

1. Democratizing Space Science for Students & Enthusiasts: Giving learners a hands-on, intuitive sandbox to explore deep-space data without needing supercomputers or advanced coding skills.  

2. Accelerating Research for Scientists: Lifting the heavy data-wrangling burden so researchers can rapidly isolate spectral anomalies, compare temporal shifts, and map water/ice distributions.  

Creativity & Accessibility Factors Considered

To make cosmic data truly inclusive and engaging, our team incorporated several creative features and human-centric design factors:

 Spectrum Sonification (Web Audio API): Converts light spectra into audio frequencies, allowing visually impaired users and researchers to "hear" cosmic anomalies and absorption dips.  

 Bilingual & Inclusive UI: Designed with a space-inspired dark theme, full mobile responsiveness, and native Right-to-Left (RTL) Arabic support alongside English to bridge the language gap in space education.  

 Citizen Science Micro-Tasks: Includes a lightweight voting system (⁠localStorage⁠ / ⁠SQLite⁠) where volunteers can help validate AI-flagged candidates.  

 Transparency & Rapid Prototyping: Because full-scale SPHEREx public archives are rolling out, we engineered a synthetic spectral cube generator (⁠prepare_data.py⁠)—clearly labeled as Synthetic / Demo Data in the UI—to validate our pipeline ahead of direct integration with the NASA/IPAC IRSA archive via ⁠astroquery⁠.  

Tools, Coding Languages & Architecture

 Programming Languages: Python 3.14.3, TypeScript 5.6, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3, and PowerShell.  

 Backend & Scientific Computing: FastAPI and Uvicorn (RESTful API & ASGI server), Pydantic (data validation), NumPy 2.5.4 & SciPy 1.18 (102×128×128 spectral cube math), Astropy 7.0+ (FITS handling & astronomical calculations), Astroquery 0.4.9 (NASA/IPAC IRSA archive integration), scikit-learn 1.5+ (Isolation Forest anomaly detection), and SQLite.  

 Frontend & Visualization: React 18.3, Vite 5.4, Tailwind CSS 3.4, Plotly.js 2.35 (3D cubes, heatmaps, and spectral plots), HTML5 Canvas API (real-time RGB/band rendering), Web Audio API (spectrum sonification), and Lucide-React.  

 Data Formats & Deployment: Compressed Binary Float32 (⁠.bin⁠) cubes, JSON metadata, Docker/Docker-Compose, Vercel (Frontend), and Render/Railway (Backend).
